proposals.evidence: DEDR2495 gives Malayalam cikkiṇi young/small, Kannada ciga little/small and Tulu cikini tender/young/small. Belari sigɨṇi a little is a qualified s-g-nasal formation comparison: retain voiced g, medial ɨ and retroflex ṇ rather than normalize to any one comparandum. DEDR1603 has kinni/kinkana but lacks the initial s/c series, making2495 the better candidate. The Sanskrit/Prakrit comparisons do not establish a donor. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1148 gives Kannada/Tulu gaṭṭi hard/firm and explicitly Gondi (Ko.) gaṭṭi very, so the whole article includes an intensifying use. Belari gaṭṭiya much is a qualified extension of this gaṭṭi formation with final -ya, whose precise morphology remains unresolved. Preserve the source quantity gloss; the proposal is not justified solely by the hard/firm head. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: Bhat (1971), printed p.119 (PDF p.126), gives iḷa get up; the installed wake up gloss is compatible with DEDR851(a), whose Kannada er̤/ēr̤u includes rise and awake and Kodagu ë·ḷ- means get up. Bhat p.121 independently describes Belari ḷ corresponding to Proto-Dravidian ẓ. This is a qualified whole-family comparison: Belari high short i versus the quoted mid/long vowels remains unexplained, and no particular borrowing route is established. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
